After the capsicums have steamed for at least 15 minutes, peel off the skins and discard the stems and seeds.
Drain the peeled capsicum flesh in a sieve for 5 minutes so the dip isn't watery.

stages.title: Blend the muhammara
steps: Add the walnuts and breadcrumbs to a food processor and pulse until coarsely ground.
Add the capsicum flesh, pomegranate molasses, garlic, salt, chilli flakes, cumin and lemon juice.
Blend until thick and spreadable but still slightly textured, scraping down the sides as needed.
With the motor running, drizzle in 1 tbsp of the olive oil, then taste and add more salt or lemon juice if needed.

stages.title: Finish and serve
steps: Spoon the dip into a shallow bowl and swirl the surface with the back of a spoon.
Drizzle with the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil and serve at room temperature.

tips: Draining the roasted capsicum keeps the dip thick enough to scoop rather than runny.
Toasting the walnuts releases their oils and removes bitterness, giving a rounder, nuttier flavour.
Steaming the hot capsicums under cover loosens the skins so they peel off easily.
Pomegranate molasses varies in sweetness and tartness, so add the lemon juice gradually and taste.
variations: Stir in 1 tsp ground Aleppo-style chilli or extra chilli flakes for more heat.
Replace half the walnuts with toasted almonds for a milder, sweeter dip.
storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 5 days. Bring to room temperature before serving. Freeze for up to 2 months and thaw in the fridge overnight.

title: Japanese Kinpira Gobo
summary: Thin burdock and carrot strips stir-fried in soy, mirin and sesame until glossy.

stages.title: Prepare the burdock and carrots
steps: Scrub the burdock root under running water with a stiff brush to remove the dirt, leaving most of the skin on for flavour.
Cut the burdock into thin matchsticks about 5 cm long, then cut the carrots into matchsticks of the same size.
Fill a bowl with 1 litre water and stir in the white vinegar, then add the burdock as you cut it so it does not darken.

stages.title: Soak and drain
steps: Leave the burdock to soak in the vinegar water for 10 minutes to remove its bitterness.
Drain the burdock in a colander and pat it dry with a clean tea towel so it fries rather than steams.
Mix the soy sauce, mirin, white sugar and 1 tbsp water in a small bowl until the sugar dissolves.

stages.title: Stir-fry the vegetables
steps: Heat the vegetable oil and the sesame oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat until the oil shimmers.
Add the burdock and stir-fry for 3–4 minutes, until it smells nutty and begins to soften at the edges.
Add the carrots and stir-fry for 2 minutes, until they are bright and just tender.

stages.title: Glaze and serve
steps: Pour in the soy sauce mixture and reduce the heat to medium.
Cook for 3–4 minutes, stirring often, until the liquid has almost evaporated and the vegetables look glossy.
Take the pan off the heat, stir through the sesame seeds and serve warm or at room temperature.

tips: Soaking the burdock in vinegar water stops it browning and draws out its earthy bitterness, so the finished dish tastes cleaner.
Cut the carrots and burdock to the same thickness so both are tender at the same time and keep a slight bite.
Drying the burdock before frying lets it brown lightly instead of steaming, which gives a deeper nutty flavour.
Leaving the burdock skin on keeps the most flavour; scrub it well rather than peeling it.
variations: Add 1/2 tsp chilli flakes with the carrots for the spicy version often served in Japan.
Use parsnip matchsticks in place of burdock when it is unavailable; skip the soaking and cook for about 1 minute less.
storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Serve cold, or reheat in a frying pan over medium heat for 2–3 minutes until hot.

title: German Rotkohl
summary: Slow-braised red cabbage with apple, vinegar and warming cloves for a sweet-tart finish.

stages.title: Prepare the cabbage, apples and onion
steps: Remove the tough outer leaves from the red cabbage, cut it into quarters and cut out the core.
Shred the cabbage finely with a sharp knife and place it in a large bowl.
Peel, core and coarsely grate the apples, then toss them through the cabbage so they don't brown.
Peel the onion and slice it thinly.

stages.title: Soften the onion
steps: Melt the butter in a large heavy-based saucepan over medium heat.
Add the sliced onion and the salt, and cook, stirring often, for 5–6 minutes until soft and translucent but not browned.

stages.title: Braise the cabbage
steps: Add the cabbage and apple to the pan and stir for 2 minutes until the cabbage starts to wilt.
Add the apple cider vinegar, white sugar, whole cloves and 150 ml water, and stir to combine.
Bring to a simmer over medium heat, then reduce the heat to low and cover with a lid.
Cook for 35–40 minutes, stirring every 10 minutes, until the cabbage is very tender and deep purple-red.

stages.title: Reduce and season
steps: Remove the lid, increase the heat to medium and cook for 3–5 minutes, stirring, until most of the liquid has evaporated and the cabbage looks glossy.
Remove the cloves, then taste and add the black pepper, plus a little more sugar or vinegar if you want it sweeter or sharper.
Serve hot.

tips: Grate the apple straight into the cabbage so the acid in the vinegar and juices keeps the colour bright red-purple instead of dull blue.
Cook the onion without browning so it melts into the sauce and adds sweetness rather than a roasted flavour.
Braise covered on low heat so the cabbage softens in its own steam without scorching on the base of the pan.
Adding the sugar and vinegar together balances the sweet-sour flavour, and tasting at the end lets you adjust once the liquid has reduced.
variations: Stir through 2 tbsp of redcurrant jelly in the last 5 minutes for a fruitier, sweeter finish.
Add a bay leaf with the cloves and a splash of red wine in place of 50 ml of the water for a richer, deeper flavour.
storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 3 days, or freeze for up to 2 months. Reheat in a saucepan over low heat with a splash of water until steaming hot. The flavour improves after a day.

title: Korean Gyeran Bap
summary: Warm rice topped with a fried egg, sesame oil, soy sauce and toasted seaweed.

stages.title: Prepare the toppings
steps: Cut the nori sheets into thin strips with kitchen scissors.
Thinly slice the spring onions.
Mix the soy sauce and sesame oil in a small bowl.

stages.title: Warm the rice
steps: Place the cooked rice in a microwave-safe bowl, cover and heat on high for 2–3 minutes, stirring once, until steaming hot all the way through.
Divide the hot rice among 4 bowls and dot each with a quarter of the butter so it melts into the rice.

stages.title: Fry the eggs
steps: Heat the vegetable oil in a large non-stick frying pan over medium-high heat for 1 minute until shimmering.
Crack in the eggs, leaving space between them, and cook for 2–3 minutes until the edges are crisp and golden and the whites are set.
For runny yolks, remove the eggs at this point; for firmer yolks, flip and cook for another 30 seconds, until the yolks are cooked to your liking.
Slide one egg onto each bowl of rice.

stages.title: Finish and serve
steps: Spoon the soy and sesame oil mixture over the eggs and rice.
Scatter the nori strips and spring onions on top.
Break the yolk and stir everything together while the rice is still hot.

tips: Hot rice melts the butter and warms the yolk into a sauce, so reheat cold rice until steaming.
Frying the eggs in hot oil crisps the whites at the edges, which gives contrast with the soft rice.
Cut the nori just before serving so it stays crisp rather than going chewy.
variations: Add a spoonful of gochujang to the soy mixture for a spicy, savoury version.
Top with sautéed mushrooms or sliced avocado for a heartier bowl.
storage: Best eaten straight away. Keep leftover rice separately in the fridge for up to 1 day and reheat until steaming hot; cook fresh eggs each time.

title: Colombian Arepas con Queso
summary: Golden corn cakes with crisp edges and a soft, cheesy centre.

stages.title: Make the dough
steps: Whisk the cornmeal and salt together in a large bowl.
Pour in 300 ml warm water and 15 g of the butter, then mix with your hands until no dry patches remain.
Knead for 2 minutes until the dough is soft, smooth and doesn't stick to your hands. Add a little more cornmeal if it is sticky, or a splash of water if it cracks.

stages.title: Rest and add the cheese
steps: Cover the bowl with a clean tea towel and rest the dough for 5 minutes so the cornmeal absorbs the water.
Add the grated mozzarella and knead for 2 minutes until the cheese is evenly distributed through the dough.

stages.title: Shape the arepas
steps: Divide the dough into 8 equal portions and roll each into a ball.
Flatten each ball between your palms into a disc about 1.5 cm thick and 8 cm wide.
Pinch and smooth any cracks around the edges so the discs don't split while cooking.

stages.title: Cook the arepas
steps: Heat a large non-stick frying pan over medium heat and melt half the remaining butter (about 7 g).
Cook 4 arepas for 7 minutes on the first side, until a golden crust forms and they release easily from the pan.
Flip and cook for another 6 minutes, until golden on both sides, the cheese has melted and they sound hollow when tapped.

Transfer to a plate and wipe out the pan with paper towel. Return it to medium heat, melt the last of the butter and cook the remaining 4 arepas the same way, 7 minutes on the first side and 6 minutes on the second, until golden and hollow-sounding. Serve hot.

tips: Use precooked masarepa, not ordinary cornmeal or polenta, which will not form a dough.
Resting the dough lets the cornmeal hydrate fully, which stops the edges cracking when you shape the discs.
Medium heat cooks the arepas through and melts the cheese; high heat browns the outside before the centre is hot.
Coarsely grated mozzarella gives pockets of melted, stretchy cheese rather than a uniform dough.
variations: Split the hot arepas and fill with scrambled eggs.
Use half mozzarella and half grated feta for a saltier, tangier filling, and reduce the salt to 1/2 tsp.
storage: Best eaten fresh. Refrigerate leftovers in an airtight container for up to 2 days and reheat in a frying pan over medium-low heat for 3–4 minutes per side until hot through.

title: Israeli Sabich Pita
summary: Soft pita filled with roasted aubergine, boiled eggs, chopped salad and tangy tahini.

stages.title: Roast the eggplant
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan) and line a large tray with baking paper.
Cut the eggplants into 1 cm thick rounds and toss with the olive oil and 1/2 tsp of the salt.
Spread the slices on the tray in a single layer and roast for 30–35 minutes, turning once halfway, until deep golden and very soft in the centre.

stages.title: Boil the eggs
steps: Lower the eggs into a saucepan of boiling water and cook over medium heat for 10 minutes, until the yolks are firm and cooked through.
Transfer the eggs to a bowl of cold water and cool for 5 minutes.
Peel the eggs and slice them into rounds.

stages.title: Make the salad and tahini sauce
steps: Combine the tomatoes, cucumber and parsley in a bowl with 1/4 tsp of the salt and a pinch of black pepper.
Whisk the tahini, lemon juice, garlic and the remaining 1/4 tsp salt in a small bowl.
Whisk in 80 ml water, a splash at a time, until the sauce is smooth and pourable like thick cream.

stages.title: Warm the pita and assemble
steps: Heat the pita in a dry frying pan over medium heat for 30 seconds each side, until warm and soft, or wrap in foil and warm in the oven for 5 minutes.
Cut each pita open along one edge to make a pocket.
Fill each pita with eggplant, sliced egg and salad, then drizzle generously with the tahini sauce and serve straight away.

tips: Salting the eggplant before roasting seasons it through and helps it collapse into a silky texture rather than staying chewy.
Cooling the boiled eggs in cold water stops the cooking, which prevents a grey ring around the yolk and makes the shells easier to peel.
Add the water to the tahini gradually: it first thickens and looks split, then loosens into a smooth sauce.
Warm pita stays pliable and is less likely to tear when you stuff it.
variations: Add a spoonful of amba (pickled mango sauce) and some pickled cucumbers to each pita, if you can find them.
Swap the boiled eggs for fried eggplant slices and extra salad for a vegan version, with the pita checked for egg or dairy ingredients on the label.
storage: Best eaten straight away. Keep leftover eggplant, eggs, salad and tahini sauce in separate airtight containers in the fridge for up to 2 days and assemble just before eating.

title: Turkish Mercimek Corbasi
summary: Smooth red lentil soup scented with cumin and paprika, finished with lemon.

stages.title: Prepare the ingredients
steps: Rinse the red lentils in a fine sieve under cold running water until the water runs mostly clear, then drain.
Finely chop the onion and finely dice the carrot into 5 mm pieces so it softens quickly.
Finely chop the garlic and cut the lemon into wedges.
Measure out the tomato paste, ground cumin and paprika so they are ready to go in the pot.

stages.title: Soften the vegetables
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add the onion, carrot and salt and cook, stirring often, for 6–7 minutes until the onion is soft and translucent.
Add the garlic, tomato paste, cumin and paprika and stir for 1 minute until fragrant and the paste darkens slightly.

stages.title: Simmer the soup
steps: Add the drained lentils, the vegetable stock and 750 ml water to the pan and stir well.
Bring to the boil over high heat, then skim off any foam from the surface.
Reduce the heat to medium-low and simmer, partly covered, for 18–20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the lentils have collapsed and the carrot is very tender.

stages.title: Blend and finish
steps: Remove the pan from the heat and blend the soup with a stick blender until completely smooth, or blend in batches in a jug blender with the lid vented.
Return the soup to the pan over low heat and warm for 2–3 minutes, adding a splash of water if it is thicker than you like.
Season with black pepper and extra salt if needed, then serve hot with the lemon wedges for squeezing over.

tips: Cooking the tomato paste and spices in the oil for a minute deepens their flavour and removes the raw edge of the paste.
Blend in small batches with the lid vented if using a jug blender, because hot soup expands and can force the lid off.
Squeeze lemon in at the table, as its sharpness lifts the earthy lentils and fades if cooked for long.
variations: Melt 2 tbsp butter with 1 tsp chilli flakes and 1 tsp paprika over low heat for 1 minute, then drizzle over each bowl.
Stir 1 tsp dried mint through the soup after blending for a traditional Turkish finish.
storage: Cool and refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 3 days, or freeze for up to 3 months. Reheat over medium-low heat until steaming hot, adding a splash of water as the soup thickens on standing.

title: Mexican Tostadas de Tinga
summary: Crisp corn tostadas piled with smoky shredded chicken, chipotle tomato sauce and lettuce.
ingredients: 2 chipotle chillies in adobo, roughly chopped (from a can)

stages.title: Prepare the ingredients
steps: Thinly slice the onion and finely chop the garlic.
Roughly chop the tomatoes and the chipotle chillies.
Shred the cooked chicken with two forks, discarding any skin and bones.
Finely shred the lettuce, crumble the feta and cut the lime into wedges.

stages.title: Cook the tomato and chipotle sauce
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over medium heat. Cook the onion for 5 minutes, stirring often, until soft and lightly golden.
Add the garlic, oregano and cumin and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes and chipotle chillies and simmer over medium heat for 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until the tomatoes have broken down and are soft.
Carefully transfer the mixture to a blender and blend until smooth, then return it to the pan.

stages.title: Simmer the chicken
steps: Stir the shredded chicken and the salt into the sauce.
Simmer over medium-low heat for 10–12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce is thick, coats the chicken and the chicken is hot all the way through.
Taste and add a little more salt if needed, then remove from the heat.

stages.title: Assemble and serve
steps: Place two tostadas on each of four plates.
Spoon the hot chicken tinga evenly over the tostadas.
Top with the shredded lettuce and crumbled feta and serve straight away with the lime wedges.

tips: Chipotle chillies in adobo are very hot, so start with 1 chilli if you prefer less heat and add the second after tasting the blended sauce.
Simmering the sauce until thick keeps the tinga from turning the tostadas soggy.
Shredding the chicken finely lets it soak up more of the smoky sauce.
Assemble the tostadas only when you are ready to eat, so the base stays crisp.
variations: Replace the chicken with shredded jackfruit (drained canned young green jackfruit) for a meat-free tinga, simmering it for the same time.
Top with sliced avocado and a spoonful of sour cream to cool the heat.
storage: Keep the cooked tinga in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days or freeze for up to 2 months. Reheat in a pan over medium heat until steaming hot. Store tostadas and toppings separately and assemble just before serving.

title: French Lentil Salad with Goat Cheese
summary: Peppery green lentils tossed with mustard vinaigrette, herbs and creamy goat cheese.
ingredients: 1 bunch parsley, leaves picked and roughly chopped

stages.title: Cook the lentils
steps: Rinse the lentils under cold water and drain, then place them in a medium saucepan with the bay leaf.
Add 750 ml water and bring to the boil over high heat, then reduce to medium-low heat.
Simmer, partly covered, for 20–25 minutes, until the lentils are tender but still hold their shape.
Drain well in a sieve, discard the bay leaf and let the lentils steam dry for 2 minutes.

stages.title: Make the dressing
steps: Finely dice the shallots and place them in a large bowl with the red wine vinegar.
Leave for 5 minutes to soften and mellow the raw bite.
Whisk in the dijon mustard, olive oil, salt and black pepper until the dressing is thick and combined.

stages.title: Toss and serve
steps: Add the warm lentils to the dressing and toss to coat evenly.
Leave for 5 minutes so the lentils absorb the dressing.
Chop the parsley leaves and fold them through the lentils.
Taste and add a little more salt or vinegar if needed, then divide among 4 bowls and top with the crumbled goat cheese.

tips: Dress the lentils while they are still warm, because they absorb the vinegar and oil far better than cold lentils.
Salt the cooking water only at the end, as adding it early can toughen the lentil skins.
Soaking the shallots in the vinegar softens their sharpness so the salad tastes balanced rather than harsh.
Green or French-style lentils hold their shape; red lentils would collapse into mush.
variations: Add 2 roasted, diced beetroot and a handful of rocket for an earthy, peppery version.
Replace the goat cheese with crumbled feta and add a handful of chopped walnuts for crunch.
storage: Refrigerate the lentils and dressing, without the cheese, in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Serve cold or at room temperature and add the goat cheese just before eating.

title: Brazilian Brigadeiros
summary: Fudgy chocolate truffles made from condensed milk, cocoa and butter, rolled in sprinkles.
ingredients: 25 g butter, plus 1 tbsp extra for greasing and rolling

stages.title: Prepare the pan and plate
steps: Grease a large plate or shallow tray with some of the extra 1 tbsp butter.
Tip the chocolate sprinkles into a shallow bowl.
Combine the condensed milk, cocoa powder and the 25 g butter in a small heavy-based saucepan.

stages.title: Cook the brigadeiro mixture
steps: Place the pan over medium-low heat and stir constantly with a wooden spoon until the butter melts and the cocoa dissolves, about 2 minutes.
Keep stirring and scraping the base for 10–12 minutes, until the mixture thickens and glossy and a spoon dragged across the base leaves a trail that takes 2–3 seconds to close.
Remove from the heat and pour onto the greased plate.

stages.title: Cool the mixture
steps: Spread the mixture into an even layer on the plate so it cools quickly.
Leave at room temperature for about 40 minutes, until completely cool and firm enough to roll without sticking to your fingers.

stages.title: Roll and coat
steps: Rub your hands with the remaining butter from the extra 1 tbsp.
Scoop out about 1 tbsp of mixture and roll it into a smooth ball.
Roll each ball in the chocolate sprinkles until evenly coated.
Place the brigadeiros in small paper cases or on a tray and serve.

tips: Scraping the base constantly stops the condensed milk catching and burning, which would make the brigadeiros taste bitter.
The mixture firms up a lot as it cools, so take it off the heat when it is still soft but leaves a trail; overcooking makes the balls dry and chewy.
Buttering your hands stops the mixture sticking and gives the balls a smooth, glossy surface.
variations: Roll the balls in desiccated coconut or finely chopped peanuts instead of sprinkles.
Stir 1 tsp vanilla extract through the mixture after taking it off the heat.
storage: Keep in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days. Bring to room temperature before serving.

title: Hungarian Chicken Paprikash
summary: Tender chicken braised in sweet paprika sauce enriched with sour cream and softened onions.
ingredients: 800 g chicken thigh, bone-in or boneless, skin removed

stages.title: Prepare the chicken and vegetables
steps: Pat the chicken thighs dry with paper towel and cut each into 2–3 large pieces.
Season the chicken with the 1/2 tsp salt and a good grind of black pepper.
Finely chop the onions and garlic, and chop the tomatoes.
Pick and chop the parsley leaves and set aside for serving.

stages.title: Brown the chicken
steps: Heat the oil in a large heavy-based pot over medium-high heat.
Add the chicken in a single layer, in two batches if needed, and cook for 3–4 minutes per side until deep golden.
Transfer the chicken to a plate, leaving the fat in the pot.

stages.title: Cook the onions and paprika
steps: Reduce the heat to medium, add the onions and cook for 8–10 minutes, stirring often, until very soft and golden.
Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Take the pot off the heat for 30 seconds, then stir in the paprika and flour so the paprika doesn't burn and turn bitter.
Return to medium heat and stir for 1 minute to cook out the raw flour.

stages.title: Simmer the chicken
steps: Gradually pour in the stock, stirring to dissolve the flour and scrape up any browned bits from the base.
Add the tomatoes and return the chicken and any juices to the pot.

Bring to a gentle simmer, cover with the lid slightly ajar and cook over medium-low heat for 20–25 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through with no pink near the bone and the sauce has thickened slightly.

stages.title: Finish with sour cream
steps: Remove the pot from the heat and let it stop bubbling for 2 minutes.
Whisk the sour cream in a bowl with 3 tbsp of the hot sauce to temper it, then stir it into the pot.
Warm gently over low heat for 2–3 minutes without boiling, then taste and add salt and pepper as needed.
Scatter with the parsley and serve.

tips: Taking the pot off the heat before adding the paprika stops it scorching, which would make the sauce bitter.
Tempering the sour cream with hot sauce and keeping the sauce below a boil stops it splitting.
Browning the chicken first builds a deeper savoury base for the sauce, and the browned bits dissolve into it.
Full-fat sour cream is more stable in heat than light versions, giving a smoother sauce.
variations: Serve over buttered egg noodles or with boiled potatoes to soak up the sauce.
Add 1 sliced capsicum with the onions for a sweeter, more traditional-style sauce.
storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat gently over low heat, adding a splash of water or stock, until steaming hot throughout and without boiling. Freezing is not recommended as the sour cream may split.

title: Danish Smorrebrod with Smoked Salmon
summary: Open rye sandwiches topped with smoked salmon, lemony cream cheese, cucumber and dill.
ingredients: 1 bunch dill, fronds picked and roughly chopped

stages.title: Prepare the toppings
steps: Cut the cucumber into thin ribbons or slices with a vegetable peeler or sharp knife, then sprinkle with the salt and leave in a bowl for 10 minutes.
Finely grate the zest of the lemon, then juice half of it and cut the other half into 4 wedges.
Pick the dill fronds from the stalks and roughly chop them, reserving 4 small sprigs for garnish.

stages.title: Make the lemon dill cream cheese
steps: Beat the softened cream cheese in a bowl with a spoon until smooth.
Stir in the lemon zest, 2 tsp lemon juice and the chopped dill.
Season with black pepper and taste, adding a little more lemon juice if you want it sharper.

stages.title: Assemble the smorrebrod
steps: Pat the salted cucumber dry with paper towel to remove the liquid.
Spread each slice of rye bread thinly with butter, right to the edges, so the cream cheese does not soak in.
Spread the lemon dill cream cheese over the butter in an even layer.
Fold or drape the smoked salmon over the cream cheese in loose waves, then top with the cucumber.
Garnish each slice with a dill sprig and a grind of black pepper, and serve with a lemon wedge for squeezing over.

tips: Buttering the rye to the edges creates a barrier that keeps the bread from going soggy under the cream cheese.
Salting the cucumber draws out water, so the topping stays crisp and does not make the salmon wet.
Dense, dark rye holds up to the toppings; soft sliced bread collapses and is hard to eat with a knife and fork.
Softened cream cheese blends smoothly with the lemon and dill without lumps, so take it out of the fridge 20 minutes ahead.
variations: Replace the salmon with sliced hard-boiled eggs and thinly sliced radishes, cooking the eggs in simmering water for 10 minutes until the yolks are firm.
Swap the cream cheese for sour cream mixed with a teaspoon of horseradish-style mustard such as dijon for a sharper topping.
storage: Best eaten straight away. Keep any leftover lemon dill cream cheese covered in the fridge for up to 2 days and assemble fresh.

title: Thai Khanom Krok
summary: Small coconut-rice pancakes with crisp golden bases and soft, creamy centres.
ingredients: 1 tbsp vegetable oil, for greasing the pan

stages.title: Make the batter
steps: Whisk the rice flour, 200 ml of the coconut milk, the water, 2 tbsp of the sugar and a pinch of the salt in a bowl until completely smooth and thin like pouring cream.
Rest the batter for 10 minutes so the flour hydrates and the cooked pancakes turn out crisp rather than gritty.

stages.title: Make the coconut topping
steps: Combine the remaining 200 ml coconut milk, the remaining sugar and the remaining salt in a small saucepan.
Warm over low heat for 3–4 minutes, stirring, until the sugar dissolves and the mixture is just steaming. Do not boil.
Pour into a jug for easy spooning and keep warm. Thinly slice the spring onions and set them aside.

stages.title: Cook the bases
steps: Heat a mini pancake pan or aebleskiver-style pan with round wells over medium-low heat for 3 minutes. Brush each well lightly with the oil.
Stir the batter, then fill each well about two-thirds full. It should sizzle gently.
Cook uncovered for 3–4 minutes, until the edges are set and lift away from the pan.

stages.title: Add the topping and finish
steps: Spoon about 1 tbsp of the warm coconut topping into the centre of each pancake, then scatter over some of the spring onions.
Cover the pan with a lid or baking tray and cook over medium-low heat for 3–4 minutes, until the topping is set and the bases are golden and crisp.
Loosen each pancake with a spoon, lift out and serve warm. Oil the wells again and repeat with the remaining batter, working in batches of about 12 minutes each.

tips: Resting the batter lets the rice flour absorb liquid, which gives a crisp base and a smooth, not grainy, texture.
Medium-low heat cooks the centre through before the bottom darkens; too hot and the base burns while the topping stays runny.
Fill the wells only two-thirds full so the batter doesn't spill over when the topping is added.
variations: Scatter 1 tbsp of corn kernels over each pancake along with the spring onions for a sweeter, popular version.
Swap the spring onions for finely diced taro or a little shredded coconut for a different topping.
storage: Best eaten straight away while crisp. Refrigerate leftovers in an airtight container for up to 2 days and reheat in a 180°C (160°C fan) oven for 5 minutes.

title: Turkish Revani
summary: Tender semolina sponge soaked in lemon syrup, with a delicate citrus aroma and moist crumb.
ingredients: 80 g butter, melted, plus extra for greasing

stages.title: Prepare the tin and batter base
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Grease a 20 cm square cake tin with a little butter and line the base with baking paper.
Finely grate the zest of 1 lemon. Whisk the eggs and 120 g of the sugar with an electric mixer for 4–5 minutes, until pale, thick and doubled in volume.
Whisk in the melted butter, the yoghurt, the milk and the lemon zest until combined.

stages.title: Combine and bake
steps: Stir together the semolina, plain flour and baking powder in a bowl, then fold into the egg mixture until just combined with no dry pockets.
Pour the batter into the tin and level the top. Rest it for 10 minutes so the semolina absorbs some liquid.
Bake in the centre of the oven for 30–35 minutes, until deep golden and a skewer inserted in the centre comes out clean.

stages.title: Make the lemon syrup
steps: While the cake bakes, juice both lemons to get about 80 ml juice. Combine the remaining 180 g sugar, 300 ml water and the lemon juice in a saucepan.
Stir over medium heat until the sugar dissolves, then simmer without stirring for 8–10 minutes, until slightly syrupy.
Take off the heat and cool to room temperature, so it does not turn the cake soggy.

stages.title: Soak and rest
steps: Cut the hot cake in the tin into 16 squares or diamonds, cutting right through to the base.
Slowly pour the cooled syrup over the hot cake, a ladle at a time, letting it absorb.
Sprinkle with the desiccated coconut and rest for at least 30 minutes, until the syrup is fully absorbed and the cake is cool enough to lift out.

tips: Pour cool syrup over hot cake: the temperature contrast lets the crumb absorb the syrup evenly instead of turning gluey.
Resting the batter for 10 minutes hydrates the semolina, giving a tender crumb rather than a gritty one.
Cutting the cake before soaking creates channels so the syrup reaches the centre.
variations: Replace the zest of 1 lemon with the zest of 1 orange and use orange juice in the syrup for a sweeter, rounder flavour.
Press a blanched almond into the centre of each piece before baking for a traditional finish.
storage: Keep covered at room temperature for 1 day, or refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 4 days. Serve at room temperature or slightly chilled.

title: Portuguese Açorda Alentejana
summary: Garlicky coriander broth poured over rustic bread and topped with softly poached eggs.
ingredients: 300 g stale bread, torn into chunks
1 bunch coriander, leaves and tender stems roughly chopped

stages.title: Prepare the bread and garlic paste
steps: Tear the stale bread into bite-sized chunks and divide them among 4 wide serving bowls.
Pound the garlic with the salt in a mortar and pestle until a smooth paste forms.
Add the coriander and pound until it breaks down into a coarse green paste.
Stir in the olive oil and a good grind of black pepper.

stages.title: Heat the broth
steps: Pour the vegetable stock into a large wide saucepan and bring to a simmer over medium heat, about 6 minutes.
Stir in the garlic and coriander paste and simmer gently for 2 minutes so the flavours infuse.

stages.title: Poach the eggs
steps: Add the white vinegar to the simmering broth and reduce the heat to medium-low so it barely bubbles.
Crack the eggs into the broth one at a time, spacing them apart.
Poach for 3–4 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks are runny, or cooked through if you prefer, 5–6 minutes.
Lift the eggs out with a slotted spoon onto a plate, keeping the broth hot.

stages.title: Soak the bread and serve
steps: Ladle the hot broth over the bread in each bowl and let it sit for 1–2 minutes until the bread softens and absorbs the liquid.
Top each bowl with a poached egg and serve straight away.

tips: Use sturdy, properly stale bread, as fresh or soft sandwich bread turns to mush when the hot broth hits it.
Pounding the garlic with salt first breaks it down into a smooth paste, so it spreads through the broth without raw bites.
Vinegar in the poaching liquid helps the egg whites set quickly and stay neat.
Keep the broth at a bare simmer for poaching, as a rolling boil tears the whites apart.
variations: Add 200 g cooked prawns to the broth for the last minute, just to heat through, before ladling over the bread.
Stir a handful of baby spinach into the hot broth after the eggs are removed and let it wilt for 30 seconds.
storage: Best eaten straight away, as the bread turns soft. Keep leftover broth and eggs separately in the fridge for up to 2 days and reheat the broth until steaming before pouring over fresh bread.

title: German Kaiserschmarrn
summary: Fluffy torn pancakes caramelised in butter and sugar, served with warm berry compote.

stages.title: Make the batter
steps: Whisk the egg yolks, milk and vanilla extract in a large bowl until combined.
Add the flour and salt and whisk until a smooth batter forms with no lumps.
In a clean, dry bowl, beat the egg whites with an electric mixer until foamy, then gradually add 40 g of the caster sugar.
Keep beating until the whites hold soft peaks, then fold them into the batter in two additions until just combined.

stages.title: Rest the batter and warm the berries
steps: Leave the batter to rest for 10 minutes so the flour hydrates and the pancake turns out tender.
Meanwhile, put the berries and 1 tbsp of the remaining caster sugar in a small saucepan over medium-low heat.
Cook for 4–5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the berries are soft and juicy, then take off the heat.

stages.title: Cook the pancake
steps: Heat a large non-stick frying pan (about 28 cm) over medium heat and melt half the butter until foaming.
Pour in all the batter and cook for 5–6 minutes, until the underside is golden and the top is mostly set but still slightly wet.
Cut the pancake into quarters, flip each piece and cook for another 3–4 minutes, until golden underneath and cooked through with no raw batter in the centre.

stages.title: Tear and caramelise
steps: Add the remaining butter to the pan and use two forks to tear the pancake pieces into rough, bite-sized chunks.
Sprinkle over the remaining caster sugar and cook over medium-high heat for 3–4 minutes, turning often, until the edges are golden and caramelised.
Divide among four plates, dust with the icing sugar and serve straight away with the warm berries.

tips: Beat the whites in a clean, dry bowl, as any grease stops them from reaching soft peaks and the pancake will be dense.
Folding the whites in gently keeps the air in, which gives the torn pieces their light, fluffy centre.
Cutting the pancake into quarters before flipping makes it far easier to turn without it breaking apart.
Using medium heat prevents the base from browning before the thick batter has cooked through.
variations: Add 2 tbsp sultanas, soaked in warm water for 10 minutes and drained, to the batter before pouring it into the pan.
Serve with stewed plums instead of the berries.
storage: Best eaten straight away. Leftovers keep in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 2 days; reheat in a frying pan over medium heat for 3–4 minutes until hot.
